issues.body:
The four field encodings (ages 24/25/30/42) are byte-identical copies of AGE_OPERAND_ENC in site/src/lib/zk-prover.ts. That site file carries an explicit DRIFT GUARD note (sq-1s2.4): the values are pinned against the native encoder by crates/sparq-zk-compose/tests/site_age_enc_drift.rs.

I confirmed that guard is site-path-only: it resolves `../../site/src/lib/zk-prover.ts` (site_age_enc_drift.rs:123, :183) and parses the identifier `AGE_OPERAND_ENC` (:49, :55). The new GUI copy is at a different path AND uses a different identifier (OPERAND_ENCODING), so it is invisible to the guard on both axes — even a path-widening fix would not match the renamed symbol.

Consequence: on any circuit/encoder bump the drift test goes red, someone regenerates the site constant per the test's own remediation message, and the GUI copy silently goes stale. The GUI's live proving then fails at witness-solve time — precisely the failure the site comment warns about ('do NOT let these go stale, or the live in-browser age-gate becomes unsatisfiable'). There is no test on the GUI copy and no cross-reference comment pointing back at the guard.

This is a security-relevant committed constant (it binds the hidden value to the credential), duplicated with the guard covering only one of the two copies.
issues.fix_hint:
Preferred: do not duplicate. Hoist the map into one shared module both site/ and gui/app/ import (e.g. packages/sparq-client or a small shared lib), leaving exactly one guarded definition.

If duplication must stay, then (a) keep the identifier `AGE_OPERAND_ENC` so the existing parser matches, (b) extend site_age_enc_drift.rs to iterate over BOTH paths (site/src/lib/zk-prover.ts and gui/app/src/lib/zk-prover.ts), asserting each parses non-empty (the test already has a non-vacuous guard for this) and matches native_enc, and (c) carry the site file's DRIFT GUARD comment into the GUI copy with a pointer to the test.
issues.title: Committed operand_enc constants duplicated outside the native drift guard (renamed OPERAND_ENCODING)

issues.body:
proveAge() performs the full cold start inline on each invocation: the Promise.all dynamic imports + circuit fetch, then `await bb.Barretenberg.new({ threads: 1 })` and `new bb.UltraHonkBackend(...)`.

The source this was extracted from deliberately does not do this. site/src/lib/zk-prover.ts memoizes the whole thing behind a single shared `proverPromise` in loadProver(), documents `Barretenberg.new` as 'the dominant cold cost', exposes prewarmProver() so the route can pay it off-click, and resets the promise on failure to allow retry. None of that survived the extraction.

Two consequences:
- Every click re-pays the dominant cold start (WASM instantiate) plus a redundant circuit re-fetch, so each proof after the first is needlessly slow. The panel has no pre-warm, so the first click pays it on the render path too.
- Nothing releases the previous Barretenberg instance. Each proof allocates a fresh WASM instance (and its worker/memory) that is dropped on the floor, so repeated proving in a long-lived workbench tab accumulates them. This is a leak, not just a perf regression — and the workbench is a persistent-tab app, unlike the site's one-shot demo page.

The module-level `basePath()` import and the per-call fetch also mean a transient fetch failure has no cached-failure reset semantics.
issues.fix_hint: Port loadProver()'s shared-promise pattern: hold a module-level `proverPromise` caching { Noir, backend, circuit }, reuse it across calls, and reset it to null in a .catch so a transient fetch/instantiate failure can be retried. Optionally export a prewarm() the ZkTool calls in a mount effect. If a per-call backend is genuinely wanted, explicitly release the instance in a finally block instead of leaking it. Simplest and best: import the shared implementation rather than re-deriving it.
issues.title: Prover context is rebuilt on every proof: new Barretenberg WASM instance per click, never released

issues.body:
`total` is reduced modulo FIELD_P (2_147_483_647) at every step of the reduce, then compared directly: `verdict: total >= threshold`. Modular reconstruction is only faithful to the real sum when that sum is < FIELD_P, and nothing in the code or the UI enforces that.

Concrete counterexample: two parties with value 1_100_000_000 each and threshold 2_000_000_000. True sum is 2_200_000_000, which is >= the threshold, so the honest verdict is true. But 2_200_000_000 mod 2_147_483_647 = 52_516_353, so the function returns verdict === false. The revealed bit — the single thing this tool exists to reveal — is wrong, with no error and no warning.

The inputs are unbounded on both paths:
- mpc-tool.tsx feeds `Number(event.target.value)` from free-form <input type="number"> fields (min=0 is not enforced on paste/programmatic entry and does not cap the upper end at all).
- workspaceIntegers() accepts anything passing Number.isSafeInteger, i.e. up to 2^53-1, and loadWorkspaceValues() pushes up to 8 of those straight into `values`.

Individual party values >= FIELD_P are also silently reduced by `mod(value - sum)` in the share construction, so a single large value is misrepresented before any summing happens.
issues.fix_hint: Validate inputs against the field: reject (or clamp with a visible error) any party value < 0 or >= FIELD_P, and reject when parties.length * (FIELD_P - 1) could overflow the intended range — practically, assert the plaintext sum < FIELD_P before returning a verdict and throw/surface an explicit 'inputs exceed the simulation field' error otherwise. Compute the verdict from the plaintext sum for the honesty check, or widen to BigInt with a larger modulus. Add a regression test pinning the counterexample above.
issues.title: Threshold verdict is computed on the mod-p total, so any true sum >= FIELD_P silently returns the wrong answer

issues.body:
The first test makes three assertions: verdict === true, shares.length === 2, localSums.length === 2. The two length assertions are structural only. The single behavioural assertion does not constrain the sharing logic:

- A trivially broken implementation that emitted `row = [0, value]` (no randomness, no field arithmetic, nothing secret-shared) would produce total = 110 and still pass this test green. The additive-sharing construction — the entire point of the module — is therefore untested.
- The below-threshold branch is never exercised. `total >= threshold` could be inverted to `<` and only this one case would flip; there is no test asserting verdict === false for a sum under the threshold.
- The documented precondition `if (parties.length < 2) throw` has no test.
- localSums is asserted only by length. It is also never read by mpc-tool.tsx (only `result.shares` and `result.verdict` are rendered), so it is currently dead output with no behavioural coverage anywhere.
- The injected `random` seam is passed (`() => 0.25`) but no assertion depends on the resulting share values, so the determinism the seam exists to provide is unused.

The workspaceIntegers test is fine — it genuinely pins dedup and ordering.
issues.fix_hint: Add assertions that actually pin the invariants: (1) each share row sums to that party's value mod FIELD_P; (2) the sum of localSums mod FIELD_P equals the plaintext total; (3) a below-threshold case asserting verdict === false; (4) assert.throws for a single-party input; (5) with the fixed random seam, assert the concrete expected share matrix so a change in the construction goes red. Then confirm the suite goes RED when `>=` is flipped to `<` and when the sharing is replaced by [0, value].
issues.title: Test does not pin the load-bearing invariants: no false branch, no reconstruction check, passes under a broken sharing

issues.body:
The done-state block renders unconditionally:

  <CheckCircle2 className="size-4 text-[var(--success)]" aria-hidden />
  Verification: {state.verified ? "accepted" : "rejected"}

The icon and its success colour are outside the ternary, so when verified === false the panel shows a green success checkmark immediately adjacent to the word 'rejected'. The surrounding container styling is also unchanged between the two cases. The AlertTriangle/destructive treatment is reserved for the `error` state (a thrown exception) and is never reached by a proof that verifies false.

On a ZK surface this is the wrong direction to fail. A failed cryptographic verification is the one outcome the panel must not dress up as success — a user glancing at the green check reasonably reads it as 'the proof checked out'. The site's equivalent flow is not reviewed here, but this panel is what the sq-ixc3.17 tier flip promotes to `built: true` / `tier: live-bbjs`, so it is the honesty-bearing surface.

Minor related point in the same block: `state.eligible` is rendered as the raw String(boolean) under the label 'Disclosed predicate', which is honest but terse given `verified` and `eligible` are independent bits users are likely to conflate.
issues.fix_hint: Branch the icon, colour and container on state.verified: render CheckCircle2 with var(--success) only when verified === true, and AlertTriangle with the destructive treatment when verified === false. Consider treating verified === false as a distinct prominent state rather than a field inside the success card, since with a correct circuit it should be unreachable and therefore indicates something is wrong.
issues.title: A REJECTED verification renders a green success check icon

issues.body:
Two claims in this panel are stronger than the code behind them.

1. The badge reads 'Simulation · honest-majority semi-honest'. That names a specific cryptographic adversary model, but simulateThreshold runs entirely inside one browser tab in one process: there are no parties, no channels, no adversary, and therefore no threat model to be honest-majority or semi-honest with respect to. Attaching the label to an in-memory illustration invites the reader to transfer the native sparq-mpc protocol's (already semi-honest-only) security posture onto something that has none.

2. The header says the tool will 'Secret-share integer inputs and reveal only whether their sum meets a threshold.' The implementation does not do that: mpc-sim.ts reconstructs the full plaintext total (`const total = localSums.reduce(...)`) and then merely chooses to display only the boolean. A real threshold protocol never materialises the sum. The distinction matters because 'reveal only X' is a privacy claim, and here the sum is computed in the clear and simply not printed.

Credit where due: the prose paragraph below the header is genuinely good and does most of the honesty work ('in-tab additive-sharing illustration, not the native sparq-mpc protocol and not live networked MPC'), and tier `live-sim` is the correct taxonomy value. The fix is to bring the badge and header in line with that paragraph.
issues.fix_hint: Drop the adversary-model wording from the badge — 'Simulation · illustrative only' or 'Simulation · no security model' is accurate. Reword the header to describe what actually happens, e.g. 'Additively secret-share integer inputs and reconstruct their sum to evaluate a public threshold', so no 'reveal only' claim is made. If the 'reveal only the bit' property is wanted for real, the comparison must be performed without reconstructing the total.
issues.title: Badge asserts a specific adversary model, and the header claim overstates what the simulation withholds

issues.body:
Both new panels do this (zk-tool.tsx workspaceAges, and the identical pattern in mpc-tool.tsx workspaceValues):

  React.useMemo(() => workspaceIntegers(snapshotStore() ?? ""), [snapshotStore, storeSize])

Two problems.

(a) Wrong invalidation key. engine-context.tsx documents storeEpoch as the content-change signal — 'monotone within a session; carries no content itself — pair with snapshotStore' (engine-context.tsx:459) — and it is bumped whenever the base store content changes (:784). storeSize is a quad COUNT. Any mutation that preserves the count (a replace, a clear-then-reload of equal size, an edit that swaps a literal's value) leaves the memo stale, so the panel shows integers that are no longer in the store. Every existing caller uses storeEpoch for exactly this reason (streaming-tool.tsx:188, :326).

(b) Render-path cost. snapshotStore() serializes the ENTIRE dataset to N-Quads (engine-context.tsx:1465, storeToNQuads), and this runs synchronously during render, then regex-scans the whole string. Every other caller does it inside an effect or a user-triggered callback (streaming-tool.tsx:183, import-drawer.tsx:241), never on the render path. On a large store, merely opening the ZK tab blocks the UI to build a hint sentence the user did not ask for — and in zk-tool the entire result is used only to render one advisory line.
issues.fix_hint: Swap storeSize for storeEpoch in both dependency arrays. Move the serialization off the render path into a useEffect + useState (matching streaming-tool.tsx's pattern), or compute it lazily behind the existing 'Use live workspace integers' button rather than eagerly on mount.
issues.title: Whole-store N-Quads serialization runs synchronously in useMemo, keyed on the wrong change signal

issues.body:
The extraction inlines `const options = { verifierTarget: "evm" as const }` with no explanation. The source file it was copied from wraps the same value in an explicit warning that is load-bearing for the ZK property (site/src/lib/zk-prover.ts, PROOF_OPTIONS):

  - 'We NEVER pass any *-no-zk flavour: those set disableZk:true and strip the ZK masking, which would make the private age recoverable in principle.'
  - '⚠️ @aztec/bb.js is pinned to a NIGHTLY. The verifierTarget option surface can shift between nightlies — RE-TEST this flavour ... on ANY bb.js version bump before trusting it.'

The GUI copy carries neither. package.json here does pin the same nightly (@aztec/bb.js 5.0.0-nightly.20260324) as a runtime dependency of the GUI app, so the nightly caveat now applies in a second place with the warning present in only one. A future maintainer editing this file has no signal that the flavour string is security-relevant rather than cosmetic.

Also: this module has no unit test and was not added to the test:unit list (only mpc-sim.test.ts was). The pure, cheaply-testable parts — the operand lookup and its throw, and the padStart/charCodeAt digit encoding — are uncovered, despite the digit encoding being exactly the kind of off-by-one that silently produces an unsatisfiable witness.
issues.fix_hint: Carry the PROOF_OPTIONS comment block (or a one-line pointer to it) into the GUI copy. Add a small zk-prover.test.ts covering: proveAge throws for an age with no committed encoding; the digit encoding for each of the four provable ages matches the expected ASCII pair; AGE_THRESHOLD/PROVABLE_AGES agree. Register it in the test:unit script alongside mpc-sim.test.ts. This becomes unnecessary if the shared-module consolidation from the first issue is done instead.
issues.title: verifierTarget flavour copied without its safety note; bb.js pinned to a nightly with no re-test guard

verdict.summary:
PR #5318 promotes the ZK and MPC workbench tools from honest stubs to live panels by extracting the site's real bb.js/Noir UltraHonk prover into gui/app and adding a new additive-sharing MPC simulation. The proving mechanics are genuinely real and the panels carry reasonable honesty caveats (research-track/not-externally-audited badge, live-bbjs / live-sim tiers, an explicit 'not the native sparq-mpc protocol' note), so the privacy-claims posture is broadly right. But the extraction is a lossy copy of site/src/lib/zk-prover.ts that drops two load-bearing safeguards, and the new MPC simulation has a demonstrable wrong-answer bug its test does not catch.

Blocking themes:
1. The four committed operand_enc encodings are duplicated into gui/app/src/lib/zk-prover.ts under a NEW identifier (OPERAND_ENCODING), placing them outside crates/sparq-zk-compose/tests/site_age_enc_drift.rs, which hard-codes the site path and parses AGE_OPERAND_ENC. The GUI copy can silently go stale on an encoder bump; live proving then breaks.
2. The shared prover context (loadProver/prewarmProver) was dropped: every click re-fetches the circuit and instantiates a fresh Barretenberg WASM backend (the site documents this as the dominant cold cost) with nothing releasing the previous one.
3. mpc-sim.ts derives the verdict from the mod-p reconstructed total, so any true sum >= FIELD_P wraps and returns a wrong verdict; counterexample below.
4. mpc-sim.test.ts asserts only verdict===true and two array lengths — no below-threshold branch, no reconstruction check; it still passes under a trivially broken sharing.
5. zk-tool.tsx renders a green success check even when verification is REJECTED, and the MPC badge attaches a specific adversary model ('honest-majority semi-honest') to code with no adversary.

The sync-wasm.mjs circuit mirroring, lazy tool-panel registration, lockfile, and tier taxonomy values all check out.
